heading.en: How long until half is gone?

hook.en: Carbon dating, medicine doses and nuclear waste all use one number: the *half-life*. For a first-order process it never changes, however much you start with.

title.en: Derive t½ for zero- and first-order reactions
Use the number of half-lives to find what is left

say.en: Carbon dating, medicine doses and nuclear waste all use one number: the half-life. For a first-order process it never changes, however much you start with. In this lesson: Derive t one half for zero- and first-order reactions.
Use the number of half-lives to find what is left.
Recognise pseudo first-order reactions.

body.en: The *half-life* t½ is the time for the concentration of a reactant to fall to half its initial value. For a zero-order reaction t½ = [R]₀/2k, so it is proportional to [R]₀. For a first-order reaction t½ = 0.693/k, independent of [R]₀. After n half-lives, the fraction left is (1/2)ⁿ.
body.kn: ಅರ್ಧಾಯುಷ್ಯ ಎಂದರೆ ಕ್ರಿಯಾಕಾರಿಯ ಸಾರತೆ ಅರ್ಧಕ್ಕೆ ಇಳಿಯಲು ಬೇಕಾದ ಸಮಯ. ಪ್ರಥಮ ಕ್ರಮಾಂಕಕ್ಕೆ t½ = 0.693/k, ಆರಂಭಿಕ ಸಾರತೆಯನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. n ಅರ್ಧಾಯುಷ್ಯಗಳ ನಂತರ (1/2)ⁿ ಭಾಗ ಉಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: The half-life t one half is the time for the concentration of a reactant to fall to half its initial value. For a zero-order reaction t one half = [R] 0 over 2k, so it is proportional to [R] 0. For a first-order reaction t one half equals 0.693 over k, independent of [R] 0. After n half-lives, the fraction left is (1 over 2) to the power n. Zero order: t one half is proportional to [R] 0.
say.kn: ಅರ್ಧಾಯುಷ್ಯ ಎಂದರೆ ಕ್ರಿಯಾಕಾರಿಯ ಸಾರತೆ ಅರ್ಧಕ್ಕೆ ಇಳಿಯಲು ಬೇಕಾದ ಸಮಯ. ಪ್ರಥಮ ಕ್ರಮಾಂಕಕ್ಕೆ t one half equals 0.693 over k, ಆರಂಭಿಕ ಸಾರತೆಯನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. n ಅರ್ಧಾಯುಷ್ಯಗಳ ನಂತರ (1 over 2) to the power n ಭಾಗ ಉಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: First order: t one half equals 0.693 over k.
Fraction left after n half-lives equals (1 over 2) to the power n.
The half-life is the time for the concentration to fall to half. For first order each half-life is the same length.
First order: t half is 0.693 over k, and does not depend on the starting concentration.
Zero order: t half is R zero over 2 k, so it grows with the starting concentration.
After n half-lives, R zero over 2 to the n is left. With t half 30 minutes, after 2 hours four halvings leave one-sixteenth.
Hydrolysis of an ester in acid uses water, but water is in large excess and hardly changes. The reaction behaves as first order: pseudo first order.
On the board: half-life.

narration.en: Each molecule reacts at a random moment, but on average half of what is left reacts in every half-life t½ = 0.693/k, however much you start with. After n half-lives the fraction left is (½)ⁿ.

body.en: Some *reactions* that involve two reactants behave as first order because one reactant is present in huge excess and its concentration hardly changes. The acid hydrolysis of ethyl acetate, CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O → CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH, is one: rate = k′[ester] with k′ = k[H₂O]. The inversion of cane sugar, C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O → glucose + fructose, is another.
body.kn: ಒಂದು ಕ್ರಿಯಾಕಾರಿ ಅತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಪ್ರಮಾಣದಲ್ಲಿದ್ದರೆ ಅದರ ಸಾರತೆ ಬದಲಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಆಗ ಕ್ರಿಯೆ ಪ್ರಥಮ ಕ್ರಮಾಂಕದಂತೆ ವರ್ತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಉದಾ: ಎಸ್ಟರ್‌ನ ಆಮ್ಲ ಜಲವಿಭಜನೆ, ಕಬ್ಬಿನ ಸಕ್ಕರೆಯ ವಿಲೋಮನ.

problem.en: A first-order reaction has k = 0.0693 min⁻¹. Find its half-life and the fraction of reactant left after 40 minutes.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A first-order reaction has k = 0.0693 min⁻¹. Find its half-life and the fraction of reactant left after 40 minutes.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A first-order reaction has k equals 0.0693 minutes to the power minus 1. Find its half-life and the fraction of reactant left after 40 minutes.
t one half equals 0.693 over k equals 0.693 over 0.0693 equals 10 minutes.
40 minutes equals 4 half-lives.
Fraction left equals (1 over 2) to the power 4 equals 1 over 16 equals 6.25 percent.
So the answer is t one half equals 10 minutes; 1 over 16 left.

problem.en: A radioactive isotope has t½ = 5 min. How much of a 100 g sample remains after 20 min?

steps.en: Radioactive decay is first order. 20 min = 20/5 = 4 half-lives.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A radioactive isotope has t½ = 5 min. How much of a 100 g sample remains after 20 min?

say.en: Let us solve this together. A radioactive isotope has t one half equals 5 minutes. How much of a 100 grams sample remains after 20 minutes?
Radioactive decay is first order. 20 minutes equals 20 over 5 equals 4 half-lives.
Remaining equals 100 times (1 over 2) to the power 4 equals 100 over 16 equals 6.25 grams.
So the answer is 6.25 grams.

body.en: For a first-order reaction, t(99.9%) = (2.303/k) log 1000 = 6.909/k ≈ 10 × (0.693/k). So 99.9% completion takes about 10 half-lives, and 99% takes about 6.64 half-lives.

homework.en: A first-order reaction has t½ = 6.93 min. How long does it take to be 99.9% complete?

narration.en: Recap. First order: t½ = 0.693/k, independent of [R]₀. Zero order: t½ = [R]₀/2k. After n half-lives, (1/2)ⁿ of the reactant is left. Ester hydrolysis in excess water and inversion of cane sugar are pseudo first order.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಪ್ರಥಮ ಕ್ರಮಾಂಕ: t½ = 0.693/k. ಶೂನ್ಯ ಕ್ರಮಾಂಕ: t½ = [R]₀/2k. n ಅರ್ಧಾಯುಷ್ಯಗಳ ನಂತರ (1/2)ⁿ ಉಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಎಸ್ಟರ್ ಜಲವಿಭಜನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸಕ್ಕರೆ ವಿಲೋಮನ ಹುಸಿ ಪ್ರಥಮ ಕ್ರಮಾಂಕದವು.

title.en: Temperature dependence of the rate: Arrhenius equation
title.kn: ಕ್ರಿಯಾದರದ ಮೇಲೆ ತಾಪಮಾನದ ಪ್ರಭಾವ: ಆರ್ಹೇನಿಯಸ್ ಸಮೀಕರಣ

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. First order: t one half equals 0.693 over k, independent of [R] 0.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಪ್ರಥಮ ಕ್ರಮಾಂಕ: t one half equals 0.693 over k.

say.en: Zero order: t one half = [R] 0 over 2k.
say.kn: ಶೂನ್ಯ ಕ್ರಮಾಂಕ: t one half = [R] 0 over 2k.

say.en: After n half-lives, (1 over 2) to the power n of the reactant is left.
say.kn: n ಅರ್ಧಾಯುಷ್ಯಗಳ ನಂತರ (1 over 2) to the power n ಉಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Ester hydrolysis in excess water and inversion of cane sugar are pseudo first order.
say.kn: ಎಸ್ಟರ್ ಜಲವಿಭಜನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸಕ್ಕರೆ ವಿಲೋಮನ ಹುಸಿ ಪ್ರಥಮ ಕ್ರಮಾಂಕದವು.
